components: Event sourcing: commits a business change

steps: A command is validated against current aggregate state.
The resulting domain event E12 appends immutably with expected stream version.
Projectors consume E12 to update derived views.
Replay from events or a snapshot reconstructs the same aggregate state.

lesson.scenario: A community bank reconstructs account A-12 from immutable deposits, withdrawals, and a snapshot.

steps.title: Load snapshot and tail
steps.narration: The handler loads snapshot v20 at $800, then replays a $100 deposit and $60 withdrawal.
steps.outcome: Current aggregate state is derived, not read from a mutable authoritative row.
steps.invariant: Replaying the same ordered facts produces the same account state.

steps.title: Validate the command
steps.narration: Withdrawal W-9 requests $200; the reconstructed $840 balance satisfies the no-overdraft rule.
steps.outcome: Business validation uses reconstructed aggregate state.
steps.invariant: Commands express intent; only accepted outcomes become immutable events.

steps.title: Append with expected version
steps.narration: MoneyWithdrawn $200 appends as v23 only if the stream is still at expected version 22.
steps.outcome: Optimistic concurrency prevents two writers from silently forking A-12.
steps.invariant: Events append; previously committed account facts are never updated in place.

steps.title: Update the projection asynchronously
steps.narration: The projector consumes v23 and writes the query-optimized balance.
steps.outcome: The read model catches up from $840 to $640 and can be rebuilt if corrupted.
steps.invariant: Projection handlers are idempotent and checkpoint only after applying an event.

steps.title: Rebuild from history
steps.narration: A repair clears the projection and replays through v23, reproducing $640.
steps.outcome: Immutable history repairs the derived view and supports new projections.
steps.invariant: Snapshots optimize replay but never replace the authoritative event stream.
